title: 2026 waste-battery emissions monitoring and limits QA controls

sources.title: Waste batteries: appropriate measures for permitted facilities
Waste batteries: emissions monitoring and limits appropriate measures

facts.source_fact: Permitted waste-battery facilities must create and maintain an inventory of point-source emissions to air and water including sewer.
facts.expected_handling: Require an emissions inventory before applying substance-specific monitoring rules.

facts.source_fact: The air-emissions inventory must include flow and temperature averages and variability.
facts.expected_handling: Carry flow and temperature characteristics with air-emission records.

facts.source_fact: The air-emissions inventory must include average concentration and load values and their variability for relevant substances.
facts.expected_handling: Keep concentration and load metrics distinct and include variability.

facts.source_fact: The air-emissions inventory should include flammability, explosive limits, reactivity and substances affecting treatment or plant safety.
facts.expected_handling: Add safety/reactivity context before selecting monitoring or abatement rules.

facts.source_fact: Monitoring locations must meet MCERTS standards and monitoring must use qualified accredited methods and certified staff.
facts.expected_handling: Require MCERTS-compatible location, method and personnel provenance.

facts.source_fact: Emissions monitoring must be carried out when the plant is operating at or near full treatment capacity.
facts.expected_handling: Record operating capacity at sampling time and reject unqualified low-load comparisons.

facts.source_fact: Plant treatment processing rate and air-flow rate at monitoring time must be recorded and submitted with results.
facts.expected_handling: Bind monitoring results to contemporaneous process-rate and airflow data.

facts.source_fact: Channelled dust monitoring uses EN 13284-1 every 6 months with a 5 mg/m3 emission limit unless the permit states otherwise.
facts.expected_handling: Attach standard, frequency and permit-specific override status to dust records.

facts.source_fact: Relevant TVOC monitoring uses EN 12619 every 6 months with a 30 mg/m3 emission limit unless the permit states otherwise.
facts.expected_handling: Apply TVOC rules only when relevance is established by the emissions inventory.

facts.source_fact: Relevant hydrogen fluoride monitoring uses CEN TS 17340 every 6 months with a 1 mg/m3 emission limit unless the permit states otherwise.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve HF method, frequency and limit together.

facts.source_fact: Relevant sulphur dioxide monitoring uses EN 14791 every 6 months with a 150 mg/m3 emission limit unless the permit states otherwise.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve SO2 method, frequency and limit together.

facts.source_fact: Relevant ammonia monitoring uses EN ISO 21877 every 6 months with a 10 mg/m3 emission limit unless the permit states otherwise.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve ammonia method, frequency and limit together.

facts.source_fact: PFOA/PFOS and other relevant PFAS have annual air-monitoring requirements using specified US EPA methods or alternatives agreed by the Environment Agency.
facts.expected_handling: Require PFAS relevance and agreed analytical method before acceptance.

facts.source_fact: Periodic monitoring results should normally be the average of 3 consecutive measurements of at least 30 minutes each.
facts.expected_handling: Reject single short measurements where the guidance requires the three-measurement average.

facts.source_fact: Some parameters such as dioxins, furans and dioxin-like PCBs require a longer sampling period, including a single period of at least 6 hours.
facts.expected_handling: Carry parameter-specific minimum sampling duration.

facts.source_fact: Monitoring frequencies may be reduced if emissions are demonstrated to be sufficiently stable over time.
facts.expected_handling: Require documented stability evidence before lowering frequency.

facts.source_fact: Relevant water or sewer emissions require monitoring of key process parameters such as flow, pH, temperature, conductivity or BOD at key locations.
facts.expected_handling: Bind water results to location and process-parameter context.

facts.source_fact: Direct discharges to water require monthly monitoring of either TOC using EN 1484 with 60 mg/l limit or COD using ISO 6060 with 180 mg/l limit unless the permit states otherwise.
facts.expected_handling: Enforce the TOC-or-COD choice and retain the selected standard and limit.

facts.source_fact: Total suspended solids are monitored monthly to 60 mg/l and hydrocarbon oil index monthly to 10 mg/l using the stated standards unless the permit states otherwise.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve pollutant-specific method, frequency and limit.

facts.source_fact: Metals, metalloids, PFOA/PFOS and other PFAS have substance-specific water monitoring requirements when identified as relevant by the emissions inventory.
facts.expected_handling: Do not apply conditional pollutant limits without an inventory-based relevance decision.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited source fact without broadening its scope.
Apply limits and frequencies with permit overrides and emissions-inventory relevance.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents applying generic limits where permit-specific requirements differ.

guard_patterns.handling: Carry monitoring standard, sampling duration, frequency and MCERTS context.
Carry source URL, publisher and monitoring method into derived outputs.
Do not convert facility monitoring rules into parcel-level measured emissions without a separate parcel-binding gate.

generation_rule: CARTESIAN_PRODUCT facts x guard_patterns; control_id={package_id}_{fact_id}_{pattern_id}; each generated row inherits confidence_percent=99 and verification=PASS
